problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.gist: A sign-maker wants to know whether a slogan s reads the same in both directions. First turn every upper-case letter into lower case and throw away every character that is not a letter or a digit. If what remains reads the same forwards and backwards, the slogan is a palindrome.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.gist: You get an integer array height of length n. Picture n vertical posts on a number line: post i stands at x = i and runs from (i, 0) up to (i, height[i]). Choose two posts; together with the x-axis they form a tank.

problems.title: 3Sum

gfg.why: only asks whether a zero-sum triplet exists
target x instead of 0, existence only

problems.gist: You are given an integer array nums (think of it as a list of ledger entries). Return every distinct triplet [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] with i != j, i != k, j != k and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.

problems.title: Sort Colors
problems.gist: You get an array nums of n items, each painted red, white or blue, written as the integers 0 (red), 1 (white) and 2 (blue). Rearrange the array in place so that equal colours are next to each other, in the order red, white, blue (all 0s, then all 1s, then all 2s).

problems.title: Merge Sorted Array
problems.gist: Two sorted lists of sensor readings must be combined. The first array nums1 has room for both: its first m entries are real readings in non-decreasing order, and its last n entries are placeholders (they hold 0 and must be ignored).

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
problems.gist: A sensor log gives an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order. Remove the repeated readings in place so that each distinct value appears once, keeping the original (sorted) order. Let k be the number of distinct values.

problems.title: Valid Palindrome II
problems.gist: You get a string s. Return true if s can be made a palindrome by deleting at most one character (deleting none is allowed), and false otherwise. A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards.

problems.title: Move Zeroes
problems.gist: A shelf scanner writes one reading per slot into an integer array nums; a reading of 0 means "empty slot". Rearrange the array in place so that every zero ends up at the end, while all the non-zero readings keep their original relative order. Do not allocate a copy of the array.

problems.title: Valid Word Abbreviation
problems.gist: A word can be abbreviated by replacing any number of non-adjacent, non-empty substrings with their lengths. The lengths are written in decimal with no leading zeros.
